title: Authentication and authorisation: the difference everyone confuses

videos.script: Two questions sound alike and are not. Who are you? And what may you do? {{two}} The first is authentication. The second is authorisation. Mix them up and you get the most common access flaw on the web: a system that checks who you are and then lets you do anything. {{flaw}} The lab's portal answers both, and you will hear each answer. A stranger hears sign in first. ana, signed in, asking for bruno's payslip, hears not yours to read. {{answers}} Then you will read the six lines of code that decide it, and see why the order of two checks hides which payslips exist. {{code}} Last, the common ways to organise permissions, from owners to roles to attributes. {{models}}
